origin.details: The same function as has_attr. A function has the attribute when that name is in its attributes, including the failure handler stored as fail.
origin.example:
has_attr(has_attr, "fail")
x <- 10
x %has_attr% "a"

y <- list(a = 1, b = 2)
see_if(y %has_name% "c")

translation.details: The same function as has_attr. A function has the attribute when that name is in its __dict__, including the failure handler stored as fail.
translation.example:
from assertthat import has_attr, see_if

print(has_attr(has_attr, "fail"))
x = 10
print(see_if('x %has_attr% "a"'))

y = {"a": 1, "b": 2}
print(see_if('y %has_name% "c"'))
